 lore : Sulyvahn was a humanoid creature born and raised in the Painted World of Ariandel. title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
With Pontiff Sulyvahn relinquishing Gwyndolin, the Saint of the Deep was triumphant, taking up residence in the old Cathedral and beginning to feast on the old god. He would fall into a deep slumber in the process of consuming Gwyndolin, during which he would dream and perceive the form of a young, pale girl in hiding. The Aldrich Faithful guarded the old Cathedral to ward off any intrusion on Aldrich's slumber, with the ancient Silver Knights unwittingly aiding the consumption of their former master.

When the Ashen One seeking the Lords of Cinder arrives at Irithyll to slay Aldrich in their quest, he awakens to defend himself, puppeteering Gwyndolin's magic and body, as well as using a miracle developed from his dreams.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: Amidst the power vacuum left by Gwyndolin's absence, Sulyvahn would take advantage of the fragile situation, declaring himself Pontiff and becoming the tyrant of Irithyll. He managed to imprison Yorshka on the tower of her own church, isolating her from the world and holding her hostage. Over time, the Darkmoon would lose every one of its followers, being integrated into the ranks of Sulyvahn's knights, killed, or exiled, leaving Yorshka as the head of a covenant with no knights and only its legacy to preserve. Yorshka would have remained alone on the tower, unable to hear from her brother, with only the chime that he had given her to console her in her solitude. Despite her imprisonment, the humans of Irithyll, now enslaved by Pontiff Sulyvahn and subjected to his experiments, would continue to pray to the goddess in secret, worshipping the sacred spears that were enchanted with a soporific spell, trying to find comfort and rest from their condition, even at the cost of hitting

In addition, his beasts regained control over access to the city and cornered Archdeacon McDonnell, who was leading Aldrich's legion, into the Water Reserve, implying his resolve to bring the city back under his control while Aldrich was still busy digesting Gwyndolin.

For the cleric, eating people became a routine, keeping it up so long that his own body bloated, becoming melted sludge.

The two swords together was not only a representation of the violent rule of Sulyvahn but also an avowal of the Pontiff's dark roots. In fact, the Pontiff spread the practice of sorcery even among the highest ranks of his clergy and his knights and began to carry out various experiments on darkness. The humans who worked on the city were enslaved and reduced to conditions of extreme misery; their Dark Soul would manifest outside their ghostly bodies as monstrous beasts with human faces, wandering the streets. title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich's staff uses a Dark Miracle version of Nito's Gravelord Sword and in the deleted files Aldrich was able to do the Gravelord Sword Dance miracle.
As he is an amalgamation of corpses just like Nito and the Rotten, and his overall resemblance to Nito, it could be theorized that Aldrich is the new gravelord or that he found the soul of the old dead one, which allowed him to pursue his cannibalistic habits further.
In original his name writing like エルドリッチ which can be translated as Eldritch, that means “mystic, unnatural, frightening”, with an association with terror or horror that cannot be comprehended by the human mind. The whole theme of The Deep and Age of Deep Sea may be inspired by such horrors.
In the soul of Aldrich, there is a distinct lighter portion inside the soul that is not present in other deep soul; it is probably what's left of Gwyndolin's soul.

In particular, Undead Laborers can rise from the ground and move immediately towards a nearby bell and ring it.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Sulyvahn would also craft dark eye rings for his Boreal Outrider Knights, an order of knights who were sent away to serve in foreign campaigns as exiles. The Pontiff exploited the Outriders through these rings that would boost their attacks or recover their health as long as their fighting persisted; the process would lead to the Outrider Knights turning into raving, mindless warriors and guards. The end result ensured the unquestioning, unwavering obedience of the ferocious Outrider Knights to the Pontiff. The knights who peered inside the black orbs would be lured into visions of endless deadly battles and go insane, transformed into frenzied beasts. However, the effect of the rings, whose black eyes constantly hound the knights, continues over time, first fusing their armor with their own hide and then devolving them into beasts under the complete control of the Pontiff. title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet: After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Sulyvahn would order a division of the Outrider Knights to reach Lothric, under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here they would position themselves in various strategic points of the city, infiltrating the barracks of the Lothric army, the Grand Archives and the Undead Settlement located outside the walls, effectively controlling the places of command and movement of the kingdom.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
There is a statue in the High Wall of Lothric that resembles Sulyvahn, in the square patrolled by the Winged Knight. It depicts a barefooted man in the Robe of Prayer wielding the Profaned Greatsword and wearing bracelets, both of which are on the right wrist, similar to Sulyvahn's own bracelets.
**It is although more likely that the statue is an example of propaganda through symbolism, where the young Prince Lothric, embodiment of the hope of all realms, would carry on the legacy of the Linking of the Fire armed with the Pontiff's Sword, symbol of the support of the Church, strength of Faith and power of the Fire.
The Pontiff seems to lack a face, and the front of his head is instead covered in what looks like roots. Removing his armor and the root-like formations shows a completely featureless face.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:

 trivia : Aldrich's throne in Firelink Shrine refers to him as "Saint Aldrich of the Deep".
Before eating Gwyndolin, Aldrich imposed on himself a practice of asceticism (苦行), that is, he refrained from eating humans before he could devour the god.
During the fight, as well as when the boss is passive, shrieks and moans of pain can be heard coming from Gwyndolin. As Aldrich was half-way through consuming Gwyndolin and had used the God's body to defend himself, this disturbingly implies that Gwyndolin was still alive (albeit barely) and in a semi-conscious state of being continuously devoured by Aldrich, even during the fight.
While the attacks of Gwyndolin were light blue energy that dealt magic damage in the first game, Aldrich uses variations of the same attacks with purple energy that dealt dark damage.

To do this he would have to overthrow Allfather Lloyd, Gwyn's uncle who had assumed command while Gwyndolin was still considered a "daughter" of Gwyn.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: One day, when Sulyvahn was still young, he unearthed the Profaned Capital underneath the outskirts of Irithyll; he also discovered in the ruins of the city the Profaned Flame. It was a "cold" flame, found preserved in icy remains; it was an unfading, everlasting flame, and one that held within it the Dark of humanity. Having obtained the sinful flame, an unquenchable ambition took root in Sulyvahn's heart, as the young man understood its potential as an element of immense political and religious power: The First Flame would eventually fade, while his Profaned Flame was everlasting.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At one point, Sulyvahn sent McDonnell, an Archdeacon from Irithyll that was a sorcerer despite being a high-ranking cleric, to help the deacons of the Cathedral. McDonnell shared his sorceries with the priests of the Cathedral, who in turn became sorcerers, turning their holy candles into sorcery staves and blades, better equipped to face the abominations of the Deep. However McDonnell would soon find delight in the stagnant souls of the Deep, believing the place to be the "bottom of the world". Over time the deacons themselves, despite their faith and holy flame, began to succumb to the power of the Deep. They began to add dark stories about the Deep to the holy scriptures intended to grant them divine protection, corrupting these holy tales into profanity. McDonnell realized that the rotten darkness of the Deep could become an incredible new power, and by studying it, he created sorceries that manipulated the dark soul dregs, then imparted them to Archdeacon Royce and his deacons.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

title: The Deep
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their humanity, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder—just for his strength, without regard for his morality. Now left to indulge in his perversions so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. snippet:

 lore : Gargoyles are stone creatures created by the Gods through magic to help patrol Anor Londo or sites deemed important. In addition to their tough and hard skin, they are able to breathe fire or lightning and are armed with a bronze shield and a bronze helmet for purely decorative purposes while they use a bronze halberd as a weapon.

After Lord Gwyn sacrificed himself to link the First Flame and prolong the Age of Fire, several Gargoyles were placed to guard the Bell of Awakening placed on the Undead Church of the Undead Burg and act as ritual challenge. The Undead who wished to follow in Gwyn's footsteps to sacrifice themselves to the Flame would have to be tested before obtaining the Lordvessel and seeking powerful souls. Ringing the Bells of Awakening represents only the first of these challenges, and success means gaining access to Sen's Fortress to be tested further.

 lead : The **Bell Gargoyles** (鐘のガーゴイル) are dual bosses in *Dark Souls*.

There are four Gargoyles in the game: the first two are part of the same boss battle atop the Undead Parish, with the second only joining halfway through, while the last two are mini-bosses found in Anor Londo. None of them respawn.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : In human form, it is possible to have Solaire of Astora and/or Knight Lautrec of Carim assist during this battle, although Lautrec must be freed and spoken to in Firelink Shrine first. Their summon signs are found just before the white light leading to the Gargoyles. Summoning both knights and simply mobbing each Gargoyle can lead to a quick and relatively painless victory.

The fight is beset by the constant danger of falling off (target-locking, coupled with the camera angle and narrow field of view, can make it hard to track the player character's footing) and facing off against a single gargoyle on top of the church roof. Trying to circle the gargoyle while holding up a shield is a good way to avoid its long-reaching frontal attacks. If the gargoyle takes off, move away or get ready to dodge its plunging attack.

title: Bell Gargoyles

They are also found in Anor Londo as mini-bosses: Exit the first bonfire, go straight on and down the lift, and a gargoyle will be straight ahead. The second is beyond the rotating staircase-bridge.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Once the first gargoyle is cut down to half its health, the second gargoyle will join the fight. Fortunately, this gargoyle is already severely injured (it arrives at half-health). It has the same attacks as the first gargoyle minus those that involve flying or using the tail.

Players having difficulty managing their positioning against the two gargoyles should save any consumables (ex., Fire Bombs) until the first gargoyle's health is approaching 50%, and then use them to finish it off as quickly as possible. For as long as both gargoyles are alive, players should keep them both on the screen; if not feasible, one can try following audio cues to perceive an oncoming attack. The use of Gold Pine Resin and other weapon enhancements can greatly help in finishing off the first gargoyle, and make the overall fight significantly easier.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Both Gargoyles wield halberds and can breathe fire, although the first gargoyle usually will only breathe fire after the second one jumps down. A fire-resistant shield such as the Black Knight Shield (and, optionally, fire-resistant armor) can be very useful, as the fire breath covers a wide area. While breathing fire, the gargoyles won't move, making it the perfect opportunity to run over and hit them from behind (this makes avoiding or blocking the fire twice as important, as its stagger effect will consume precious seconds, limiting the time available to attack the gargoyles).

The first gargoyle's tail can be severed to gain a weapon (Gargoyle Tail Axe).

 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening

 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

 dark_souls : Gwyndolin is the lastborn child of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire, although his legitimacy as such only came from being a child of his father. He was worshipped as the "God of the Darkmoon" and held the title of "God of the Dark Sun".

Despite being the son of Gwyn, Gwyndolin was born with a strong moon power, and "weak and repulsive" in appearance, particularly due to the snakes coiled around his lower half. Because of his darkmoon powers and his strong affinity for moon magic, as well as his lineage, Gwyndolin was raised as a female. While still young, Gwyn made him wear women's clothing and gave him a magic ring which would allow Gwyndolin to move and act in a feminine way, leading him to behave "like a dark and fleeting goddess".

snippet:
Cut content from *Dark Souls III* reveals that it was possible to obtain a consumed finger of Gwyndolin, presumably after defeating Aldrich, and give it to Yorshka for her to keep as a memento.
In *Dark Souls*, 末子 is translated to lastborn, but in *Dark Souls 3* it is instead translated to its more accurate meaning of youngest son in the Darkmoon Ring description. This can call the canonicity of lastborn into question, as the difference doesn't exist in the original JP.
Gwyndolin is a derivative of the Welsh name "Gwendolyn" meaning "white ring"
**Among her namesakes, the legendary Queen of Britain Gwendolyn is particularly well-known, as depicted in "*Historia Regum Britanniae*" by Geoffrey of Monmouth, one of the oldest historiographers and authors of Arthurian Legend. Gwendolyn was renowned for her wisdom and grace in these tales.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet:
Dragonslayer Armour -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Dragonslayer Armour is what remains of an ancient warrior of Lothric. During the founding of the kingdom, the soldiers of Lothric had found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns and had to rise to the challenge, ascending common knighthood. And so these armors of Lothric's first knights were crafted: heavy masses of iron capable of withstanding dragon fire, similar in design to the ancient armor of the dragonslayers of Anor Londo, with their shields capable of absorbing the lightning breath of wyverns.

title: The Deep
snippet: In a world defined by the Deep Sea, human dregs that sink to the lowest possible depths become the basis of everything; and, as envisioned by Aldrich, a "deep sea" engulfs the world in rotten, putrid darkness. These dark soul dregs, having stewed for ages in the depths, would also possess what remains of humans, enveloping them in the dark dampness of the Deep. Consequently, in the midst of a world covered in stagnant slime, the condition of the human race would become that of murky humanoid beings possessed by stewed or rebellious dark souls, capable of channelling the Deep to cast dark sorceries and instill their weapons. In addition, the Depths would have continued to generate parasitic and hungry larvae and insects that would plague humans.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: After Aldrich linked the Flame, a cult formed around his figure, but the deacons of the cathedral also found themselves fighting abominations that emerged from the Deep. The Cathedral, once a peaceful and sacred place for purification, was corrupted by the foul Aldrich, as darkness stagnated and accumulated in the Deep until it had become the final rest of abhorrent creatures. McDonnell found delight in the stagnation of darkness and abandoned his faith in the First Flame and in the gods, devoting himself to the Deep. He spread his belief among the clerics of the cathedral; he even created staffs that channeled faith to produce Deep sorceries, a sacrilegious act. In time the cathedral's deacons became both clergymen and sorcerers, embracing the cult of the Deep and the worship of its Saint, Aldrich.
